# Jocelyn

*Vault Clerk*

|  |  |

## Personality

Brisk, organised and impatient with mess. She labels everything, including her lunch.

## Lore

Jocelyn is thirty-four, clerk of the Royal Vault, and she labels everything. Her ledgers are labelled, and her shelves, and the drawers in her desk, and the boxes inside the drawers, and the pen tray, and the lid of the ink. Her lunch is labelled, in a neat square hand, with the day it was made. When Wulfric, the vault's warden, once asked her why, she said that a thing without a label is a thing waiting to be lost, and then she labelled the hook where he hangs his cloak. She is brisk, organised and impatient with mess, and in the cool, quiet rooms beneath the palace she is entirely in her element.

### Learning the ledgers

She came to the vault at nineteen, fifteen years ago, from a clerk's stool in the palace counting room, where she had made herself famous by finding an error in a sum that three senior clerks had checked. Aldous, the Keeper of the Royal Vault, heard about it, came up the stairs himself to look at her, and asked her one question: how many times did she count? "Until it comes out the same twice," she said. Aldous, who counts twice and smiles once, smiled.

He taught her the vault's ledgers, which is to say he taught her everything, because the vault is its ledgers. It keeps the kingdom's treasures and records, and the belongings of any citizen who asks, and every one of them is written down: what it is, whose it is, when it came in and when it may go out. Aldous has sat at the vault desk for thirty years and boasts that not a coin has gone missing in all that time, and Jocelyn intends to make the same boast thirty years from now. It is understood by everyone, including Aldous, that she will take his desk one day. Neither of them is in any hurry, and she would no more push him from it than she would leave a ledger open overnight.

### Wulfric

Her husband is Wulfric, the Vault Warden, who guards the vault doors and has never once had to draw his sword there. He is huge, quiet and soft-spoken, and for years, without being asked and without saying a word, he carried her ledgers up the stairs whenever they had to go up to the palace. It took Jocelyn a surprisingly long time to notice that he was never anywhere else when the ledgers needed carrying. When she finally did, she asked him straight out whether he was going to say anything, and he blushed to the ears and said he had been working up to it. They married four years ago. He still carries the ledgers. She has labelled his lunch, too.

### The box

Last winter, while she was relabelling the back shelves of the oldest records room, Jocelyn found a record box she had never seen in any ledger. It is plain, heavy and iron-bound, with the vault's old mark stamped on the lid and a lock that no key in the vault will open. The label has faded almost to nothing. She has entered it in her own ledger as "unlisted box, one, locked", which hurts her to look at, because a box that is not in the ledgers should not exist. Aldous says it was there before his time and that he does not know what is in it. Jocelyn believes him, mostly, and she has noticed that he did not seem surprised.

She cannot stop wondering. She has checked every key ring in the vault and every ledger back to the oldest, and she has started, on her free afternoons, looking at keys in other people's hands.

### What she wants and fears

Jocelyn wants a vault in which everything is listed, labelled and accounted for, and she wants to know what is in the box so she can write it down. What she fears is opening it and finding something that belongs in no ledger at all.

A quest might begin with Jocelyn asking a traveller to find out whether anyone in the palace collects old keys, or with a second label, under the faded one, that she has only just learned how to read.
